fieldNotes.title: Field Notes: 7 RAG implementations, 7 security audits
fieldNotes.source: Anonymous CISO at a 600-person Indian SaaS
fieldNotes.story:
Decentralization went too far. Seven product teams each shipped their own RAG implementation between Jan and June 2025. Seven different vector DBs. Seven different chunking strategies. Three different prompt-injection mitigations (one team had none).

My team had 7 attack surfaces to audit. We caught a P0 in team #4's setup — a customer's PII was being logged in plaintext to a vendor we hadn't approved. **₹47 lakh remediation. 6 weeks of rework. Trust with our enterprise clients took a quarter to repair.**

We centralized after that incident. Built a shared RAG platform with one approved vector DB, one chunking library, one prompt sanitizer. Took 4 months to migrate all 7 teams. Team velocity dropped 14% during migration. Worth every percent — we now sleep at night.
fieldNotes.takeaway: Decentralize first; centralize the moment 3+ teams duplicate the same surface. Earlier is bureaucracy; later is breach.

bossBattle.title: Boss Battle: AI Cell or AI Factory?
bossBattle.setup: Vikrant has 8 product teams, each piloting AI. Two have already shipped to customers. Three are mid-build. Three haven't started. CFO wants efficiency. Engineering wants autonomy. Vikrant has 6 weeks to decide org structure.

coach.name: Ex-CTO-now-advisor Ananth
coach.role: Built, sold, and unwound 4 AI products at scale

options.label: Decentralized — each team building their own. Right for early experimentation.
options.explain: Right. With 2 in production and 3 mid-build, decentralized was the correct first move. The question now is when to centralize.

options.label: Already centralized — they all use the same model API.
options.explain: Same API ≠ same architecture. Each team built their own infra around that API. That's the duplication risk.

options.label: Chaos — should have been centralized from day 1.
options.explain: Day-1 centralization usually ships nothing for 6 months. Decentralized first IS the right pattern.

stages.prompt: When should Vikrant centralize the AI infra?

options.label: When 3+ teams are duplicating the same surface (RAG, prompt eval, model gateway). Now might be right.
options.explain: Right trigger. Duplication ≥ 3 teams = centralize that surface. Let unique team work stay decentralized.

options.label: Centralize everything immediately to maximize efficiency.
options.explain: Premature centralization. Unique team work shouldn't be centralized just because some surfaces should be.

options.label: Centralize at the next reorg cycle, regardless of state.
options.explain: Calendar-driven centralization is bureaucratic. Trigger-driven (3+ teams duplicating) is right.

stages.prompt: Vikrant's design: a small AI Platform team (3 engineers) builds shared RAG + prompt eval + model gateway. Product teams keep their unique work. What's missing?

options.label: A governance layer — who decides what graduates from a team into the platform.
options.explain: Right. Without governance, the platform team becomes a shadow PMO. Decision rights matter more than architecture.

options.label: Nothing. The 3-engineer platform team is enough.
options.explain: Misses governance. Architecture without decision rights creates bottlenecks.

options.label: More engineers. Make platform team 8 strong.
options.explain: Over-staffing the platform team is a common over-correction. 3 is right; governance is what's missing.

outcomes.perfect: S-tier. Vikrant lands a hybrid org with explicit governance. 6 months later, 3 product teams ship faster on shared infra; the unique work stays decentralized. CISO sleeps.
outcomes.good: Solid. Architecture is right; governance layer needs another iteration.
outcomes.learn: Re-read the trigger section. The 'when' of centralization matters more than the 'whether'.
